notes: Part 1 (EINs): candidates came from the ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer API and the IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File (eo1-eo4 CSVs, fetched 2026-11-02). 'conf' shows the evidence: 'site-printed EIN' = the organization's own website prints the same EIN; 'name+city/state' = IRS name and city/state match the directory; 'name (directory has no HQ city)' = exact name only; 'none' = no EIN assigned (see x).

Government bodies (CAPAC, OHA, WA and CA commissions, DHHL, ONHR) are skipped by instruction. Smithsonian APAC, UCLA AASC and UC Berkeley AARC are typed non-government in the directory but have no IRS record under their names, so ein is null.
'arms' lists a second legal entity (e.g. 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) counterpart) and 'sponsor' a fiscal sponsor; 'unverified': true marks a link or identity the sources fetched do not settle.

Part 2 (grants): parsed from IRS e-file XML (Form 990 Schedule I RecipientTable; Form 990-PF Part XV grants paid during the year) downloaded from the IRS TEOS bulk files at apps.irs.gov. Each 'u' is the ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer full-filing page for the same IRS object id ('oid'); the page loads its schedules with JavaScript, so open Schedule I or the 990-PF statement from its menu.

'yr' is the calendar year in which the funder's fiscal year ended; 'fye' gives the exact period end date. Fiscal years differ: Kellogg ends Aug, Weingart June, California Endowment March (one filing ends Dec 2024), Carnegie Sept.

Coverage is limited to filings the IRS released in 2024-2026 (fiscal years ending 2023-2025). Earlier years were not parsed. 244 matching grant lines were found; 102 were kept: all 32 TAAF Schedule I lines to directory organizations, plus the largest or most informative lines per funder. Small payments (under $5,000) were left out.

Matching rules: Schedule I lines matched on the recipient EIN printed in the filing. Form 990-PF lines carry no recipient EIN, so they were matched on name AND city/state; same-name lines with another city were dropped (e.g. an AAJA line at a San Francisco address in a Ford filing; a Wallace line for CAPACD at an Oakland address; branch-level Boat People SOS and JACL chapter grants).

'recipient' is copied exactly from the filing, including typos and truncations (e.g. 'AMERCIAN' in Kellogg lines, a cut-off name in an Open Society line). 'purpose' is as stated, cut to 120 characters with '...' where longer. A fiscally sponsored recipient appears under the sponsor's name (Weingart: 'Community Partners FBO Empowering Pacific Islander Communities').

Silicon Valley Community Foundation is a community foundation; its filing does not say which lines were donor-advised, so treat those lines as SVCF grants without further attribution. Foundation to Promote Open Society is the Open Society Foundations entity whose 990-PF was parsed; other OSF entities were not checked.

No grant line matched in the parsed filings for these directory ids: stop-aapi-hate, jacl, asian-american-scholar-forum, aapi-data, potluck-asian-america, apapa, saalt, hindu-american-foundation, vietaid, boat-people-sos, hmong-national-development, aapi-victory-fund, chinese-american-citizens-alliance, smithsonian-asian-pacific-american-center, nextshark, south-asian-journalists-association, ucla-asian-american-studies-center, uc-berkeley-asian-american-research-center, napca, apala, nqapia, aapcho. Absence is not proof: other funders, earlier years, and fiscal-sponsor or chapter names were not searched. AAPIP's own filings show no grants to directory organizations.
ProPublica blocks scripted PDF and XML downloads with a security check, so the IRS bulk XML was the source; page images/PDFs were not read.
